chunks: My father (may Allah have mercy on him) and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan narrated from al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan ibn Aban, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Isḥāq ibn Ibrāhīm, from Hārūn ibn Khārijah, who said:

A man asked Abū ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him) while I was with him, saying, 'What is the reward for one who visits the grave of al-Ḥusayn (peace be upon him)?' He replied, 'Verily, Allah has assigned to al-Ḥusayn four thousand angels, disheveled and covered with dust, who weep for him until the Day of Judgment.' I said to him, 'May I be sacrificed for you and my mother! It is narrated from your father (peace be upon him) that (visiting his grave is equal to) Hajj and ‘Umrah?' He said, 'Yes. A Hajj and an ‘Umrah,' until he counted ten.

key_terms.زَارَ: visited (specifically referring to Ziyarah, the act of visiting the graves of Imams and saints)
key_terms.شُعْثاً غُبْراً: disheveled and covered with dust (describing the state of the angels)
key_terms.عَدَّ عَشَرَةً: he counted ten (indicating the quantity of rewards)

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for visiting the grave of Imam Husayn according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In Kamil al-Ziyarat, Ibn Qulawayh records Imam al-Sadiq’s (a.s.) declaration that the grave of Imam al-Husayn (a.s.) is attended by four thousand angels weeping until the Day of Judgment, emphasizing the perpetual spiritual presence of the martyr. When asked about the specific merit of this visitation, the Imam equates it to performing ten Hajj and ten ‘Umrah, a unique elevation of status that underscores the centrality of Karbala in Shia devotional practice and the concept of 'Hujjiyat al-Ziyarah' (the visitation itself serving as a complete act of worship).
